newsitem.title: USA: Existing homes sales rose 2.1 percent in January.
newsitem.headline: Existing homes sales rose 2.1 percent in January.

text.p: Sales of existing homes rose in January, buoyed by warm weather and low interest rates, a real estate agents' group said Friday.
The National Association of Realtors said sales of previously owned homes rose 2.1 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.94 million from a revised 3.86 million in December.
The total was higher than the 3.89 million rate forecast by economists.
The group's chief economist, John Tuccillo, tied the market's continued strength to the economy.
"The nation's economy has been steady the past year, with modest growth," Tuccillo said. "As consumers become more confident in the economy, they are more willing to make the investment in a home."
However, existing home sales for the full year would probably fall from 1996's record pace, he said.
"Our forecast for 1997 is for about a 5 percent drop from 1996 to about 3.85 to 3.90 million homes," he told reporters.
The group has factored higher interest rates in its forecasts for later this year but there was little indication that higher rates alone would badly hurt sales, Tuccillo said.
"It really hasn't affected it (the sales) very much," he said. "I think that this market is robust enough" so that it would not affect it substantially.
By region, the West posted the strongest gain, with sales up 8.4 percent. Sales rose 3.6 percent in the South, but fell 4.8 percent in the Northeast and 1 percent in the Midwest.

The average price of an existing home rose to $149,400 from $147,100 in December while the median price -- half of homes sold above it and half below -- rose to $120,500 from $118,800 in December, the group said.
A 30-year fixed-rate mortgage loan averaged 7.82 percent in January, up from 7.6 percent in December and 7.03 percent in January 1996.
The association reported a revised total of 4.09 million existing single-family home sales for last year, up from the record set in 1978 of 3.99 million units.
The supply of homes stood at 5.8 months' worth in January compared with 4.8 months in December.
